correctness.rationale: For invertible A=(a,b;c,d), nonzero idempotents correspond scheme-locally to projective roots of F_A=cX³−aX²Y+dXY²−bY³. The radial scaling equation has invertible derivative at each nonzero point, and the origin is reduced. In odd characteristic, every geometric repeated root is rational by Frobenius and cubic degree; parametrizing (X−rY)³ and (X−rY)²(X−tY) and imposing det A≠0 gives respectively (q−1)² and (q−1)³ labeled matrices. The complement has three simple roots, hence nonreduced probability 1/(q+1). For char 2 the two partial derivatives F_X=cX²+dY² and F_Y=aX²+bY² cannot share any projective zero because det A≠0. Independently enumerated all invertible prime-field q=3,5,7,11 matrices by direct discriminants and repeated-factor test; reduced/double/triple counts matched. Extension fields and all odd prime powers follow from the algebraic proof, not these finite checks.
